bug_semantics: Command_OPEN_POWERSHELL built a PowerShell -Command program by interpolating the directory of the edited file directly into a single-quoted Set-Location argument. Because an apostrophe in a Windows directory name was not escaped, a crafted path such as C:\safe'; Start-Process calc; #' terminates the string and appends attacker-chosen PowerShell. A victim need only open a file from that directory and invoke Open PowerShell or Open PowerShell as Administrator; the latter can execute after the UAC flow with elevated rights.
flaw_origin: Atomic commit 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7 changed the pre-existing PowerShell-command skeleton from a cmd.exe /k cd invocation to powershell.exe with `-NoExit -Command "Set-Location -Path '%s'"`, passing strFolder.c_str() without PowerShell single-quote escaping. That exact semantic conversion first created the injection; the immediately preceding skeleton commit still invoked cmd.exe and therefore did not contain this PowerShell parsing flaw.
ai_marker: absent — `git cat-file commit 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7` shows human author and committer Masaru Tsuchiyama <m.tmatma@gmail.com> and only the message `powershell の起動に対応`; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI trailer, bot identity, or other AI marker on the BIC commit object.
evidence: First-party developer advisory https://github.com/sakura-editor/sakura/security/advisories/GHSA-6x2x-729r-wjh5 describes the Open PowerShell/Open PowerShell as Administrator directory-as-command mechanism and records 2.4.2 as affected. JVN#74538868 at https://jvn.jp/en/jp/JVN74538868/ assigns CVE-2026-59561, states versions prior to v2.4.3 are affected, and gives the attack path: direct a victim to edit a file in a crafted directory, then arbitrary commands execute when the victim invokes Open Terminal. The developer's v2.4.3 release page explicitly lists the GHSA/JVN PowerShell injection as fixed.

In the validated clone, `git log -S 'Set-Location -Path' -- sakura_core/cmd/CViewCommander_File.cpp` returns only 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7 as the string's origin. `git log -L '/^void CViewCommander::Command_OPEN_POWERSHELL/,/^}/:sakura_core/cmd/CViewCommander_File.cpp'` likewise shows 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7 replacing `cmdExeParam.AppendStringF(L"/k cd /d \"%s\"", strFolder.c_str())` and the COMSPEC target with `cmdExeParam.AppendStringF(L"-NoExit -Command \"Set-Location -Path '%s'\"", strFolder.c_str())` and powershell.exe. Later lineage changes are comments, types, null modernization, and the eventual fix, not earlier writers of the flaw.

Direct parent verification: `git show de6749296b8b9a3ffa2c281d26758770a956f31a:sakura_core/cmd/CViewCommander_File.cpp` shows Command_OPEN_POWERSHELL still constructing `/k cd /d "%s"`, resolving COMSPEC, and launching that cmd.exe path. It has neither `Set-Location -Path` nor a powershell.exe launch, so the vulnerable PowerShell single-quoted interpolation is absent. `git show 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7` is a one-parent, non-merge atomic implementation commit whose parent is exactly de6749296b8b9a3ffa2c281d26758770a956f31a; it is not a move, revert, release commit, merge, or squash aggregate.

Fix verification: `git show 2e8716858fc58cbb98134f94ac15729765fcac2c` adds `strFolderEscaped`, replaces every `'` with `''`, and changes the format argument from strFolder.c_str() to strFolderEscaped.c_str(); the commit message explicitly identifies GHSA-6x2x-729r-wjh5 and JVN#74538868. Its parent 891340373c1e522d9efb1c5647926ece1a2190ed still passes unescaped strFolder, so 2e8716858fc58cbb98134f94ac15729765fcac2c is the direct closing fix.

Release-boundary reproduction: `git tag --contains 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7` starts at v2.4.0 (and its prereleases) and includes v2.4.1 and v2.4.2; `git grep -n 'Set-Location -Path' v2.4.0 -- sakura_core/cmd/CViewCommander_File.cpp` and the same command at v2.4.2 show the unescaped strFolder interpolation, while v2.3.2.0 has no match. `git tag --contains 2e8716858fc58cbb98134f94ac15729765fcac2c` returns v2.4.3, whose commit is fe1a4a281c6e6bec2a1a1bc39059fe7424bb5075; `git grep -n -e strFolderEscaped -e 'Set-Location -Path' v2.4.3 -- sakura_core/cmd/CViewCommander_File.cpp` shows apostrophe doubling and use of the escaped copy. Thus repository history narrows the feature-bearing vulnerable stable releases to v2.4.0 through v2.4.2 and the first fixed stable release to v2.4.3.

BIC-only AI check: raw `git cat-file commit 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7` has tree b271a68ed514bf1bfcfffb436ea95da632736719, parent de6749296b8b9a3ffa2c281d26758770a956f31a, Masaru Tsuchiyama as both author and committer, and the single ordinary subject. The 2026 fix commit does contain a Claude co-author trailer, but the audit protocol excludes AI-only-on-fix and requires judgment solely from the BIC commit object. The BIC has no AI signal.
reasoning: The causal defect is not the earlier skeleton that copied the command-prompt routine: that parent still executes cmd.exe and never submits the path to a PowerShell parser. The smallest real BIC is the next atomic feature commit, which simultaneously selects powershell.exe and embeds attacker-influenced strFolder inside PowerShell source without escaping the delimiter. The vulnerable line then persists through the v2.4.0, v2.4.1, and v2.4.2 release line until the direct security fix doubles apostrophes before interpolation and ships in v2.4.3. The BIC is an ordinary 2018 human commit with no commit-object AI attribution. Although the fix is Claude-co-authored, fix-side AI evidence is expressly out of scope, so the lifecycle is closed as NOT_AI.
